1.explanation:
1. Accordion.js – This is the top-level component where the flushAlignment prop must be declared, defaulted, and wired into the CSS className logic so that when it’s true, a modifier class (e.g. `${prefix}--accordion--flush-alignment`) is added to the <ul>.
2. AccordionItem.js – The item renders both the header and the body; it needs to detect the flushAlignment context (via props or context) and apply the matching modifier class to remove the left padding on the title and content containers.
3. Accordion.stories.js – Storybook’s playground and examples must expose the new flushAlignment prop (add it to argTypes and examples) so designers and engineers can preview and test the flush variant.
4. Accordion-test.js – The unit tests, especially the snapshot test, should be updated to include a case where flushAlignment=true to prevent future regressions and ensure the CSS modifier class is applied correctly.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshots show how the Accordion should render when the new flushAlignment prop is true. In the closed state, each AccordionItem’s title text is flush (no left padding) against the divider lines (shown by the pink highlight). In the open state, both the title and the body content are also flush against the dividers (no left indent). Currently, without a flushAlignment prop implemented, titles and body text retain the default left padding, so the component does not match the design spec.
